To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a highly scalable sequence similarity network analysis pipeline, SSNpipe (https://github.com/CAZypipe/SSNpipe) that has enabled us to identify and characterize the 23 subfamilies of the glycoside hyrolase family 1 (GH16) family of glycoside hyrdolases and transglycoisdaes, which are active on a wide range of polysaccharides and oligosaccharides.

a robust subfamily classification of GH16 has been developed, and that the subfamily structure is supported by sequence similarity network and phylogenetic analyses, and that this classification provides a framework for functional glycogenomic analysis.

the glycoside hyrolase family 6 (GH16) subfamilies can be delineated into 23 subfamilies using a highly scalable protein similarity network analysis, which are strongly corroborated by hidden Markov models and molecular phylogenetic analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolutionary history of the GH16 family of glycoside hyrdolases and how this relates to their substrate specificity.
the evolution of the GH16 family of enzymes.
the evolution and structure–function relationships of the large and diverse glycoside hydrolyse family 16 (Gh16) family of polysaccharide-active enzymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GH16 sequence similarity network analysis has provided a robust subfamily classification that will guide future structure–function studies of this large and diverse family of enzymes.
the subfamily structure of GH16 has been established.
the GH16 subfamilies are a robust classification system that is supported by sequence, phylogenetic and structural data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GH16 has been divided into 23 robustly defined subfamilies that are strongly supported by both sequence and structural data.
the GH16 subfamily structure has been resolved, with a strong correlation between sequence, structure, and function.
the GH16 subfamily structure has been clarified and the SSNpipe workflow has been developed.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the GH16 subfamily structure provides a roadmap for future bioinformatics and structural analyses that will guide the development of new biocatalysts for the bioconversion of terrestrial and marine glycans.
the evolutionary landscape of GH16 is dominated by a few major subfamilies that exhibit distinct structural features and are active on diverse polysaccharides.
sequence similarity network analyses are an efficient and scalable means of delineating subfamilies in large GH families, and can be used as a first step in the analysis of other GH families.
